claims.text: By default, queries that return entity types are tracking: the DbContext's change tracker keeps the returned entities.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Querying > Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries (Tracking queries)

claims.text: By default EF Core takes a snapshot of an entity's property values when it starts tracking it, before handing it to the application; SaveChanges compares current values with the snapshot to find changes.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Change detection and notifications (snapshot change tracking); Efficient querying > Tracking, no-tracking

claims.text: SaveChanges updates only the property values that actually changed on a tracked entity.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Change Tracking in EF Core ('Updates are limited to only those values that have actually changed')

claims.text: The snapshot takes memory and the snapshotting takes time while results load, whether or not SaveChanges is later called.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Performance > Efficient querying > Tracking, no-tracking and identity resolution

claims.text: AsNoTracking() makes a query return entities the change tracker does not keep, avoiding the change-tracking overhead in read-only scenarios.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries (No-tracking queries); Efficient querying

claims.text: AsNoTracking() does not change the SQL sent: FindAsync and FindForReadingAsync in EfOrderRepository produce the same SQL text; the saving is inside the application process.
claims.source_hint: Compare ToQueryString()/command log of the two queries at stage-2; EF Core docs: Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries

claims.text: Changing an entity loaded with AsNoTracking() and then calling SaveChangesAsync on the same context writes nothing for it, because the context does not track it.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Change Tracking in EF Core (Detached entities are not tracked); Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries

claims.text: At stage-2 EfOrderRepository.FindAsync is db.Orders.Include(o => o.Items).FirstOrDefaultAsync(...) and FindForReadingAsync is the same with AsNoTracking().
At stage-2 OrderService.CancelOrderAsync and ShipOrderAsync load the order with repository.FindAsync, call order.Cancel()/Ship(), then SaveChangesAsync.
At stage-2 OrdersController.Get calls FindForReadingAsync; Cancel calls FindForReadingAsync for the OrderOwner check, then orderService.CancelOrderAsync(id); Ship calls only ShipOrderAsync.
If Cancel called existing.Cancel() and SaveChangesAsync on the untracked copy, the response could show a cancelled order while the orders row stays unchanged.
claims.source_hint: Follows from claim 7; EF Core docs: Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries

claims.text: Use AsNoTracking() for entities that are only read to build a response, and a tracked query for entities that will be changed and saved.
A read-only endpoint returning many entities usually uses less time and memory after adding AsNoTracking(), with its SQL unchanged.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Efficient querying > Tracking, no-tracking (benchmark AsTracking vs AsNoTracking: mean and allocated)
